concepts.def: Wire with current in field feels a force.
Moving wire near magnet makes voltage.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Put a wire carrying current inside a magnetic field. The wire feels a force.

This is the motor effect.

If we coil the wire and let it spin, we have an electric motor.

Motors are in fans, drills, washing machines, electric cars, drones - everywhere!

A generator does the opposite. Move a wire through a magnetic field - and electricity is created!

This is called electromagnetic induction.

Power stations use this: steam spins a magnet, magnet spins past coils, electricity flows out. Coal, gas, nuclear, wind and hydro stations all do this same final step.

MRI scanners: a huge electromagnet maps the body without X-rays.

Maglev trains: float and zoom above a track on repelling electromagnets.

Hard drives: store data as tiny magnetic patches.

Phones: contain mini magnets in vibration motors and speakers.
